regions.locate: The opener is the last ':' (with any '-' after it) not followed by a digit; failing that the first '--', failing that the last '; -'. The list ends at the first depth-0 '.' after the opener that is not part of '...', not 'i.e.' and not '.,'. Head is before the opener, notes after the list's full stop.

(.means: In the rendering list, the provider's own sign for a word or syllable sometimes given with the principal word it is annexed to: one optional word (23,603), alternatives for that word (9,177), a suffix syllable (9,589) or a prefix syllable (2,526); or the provider's note on an irregular rendering ('from the margin', 'by mistake for ...', a citation: 527). In the definition head it is an aside in Strong's own sentence (174); after the list it wraps a note (77). It never divides a reading, and a group is never distributed across its head.
(.evidence: אדבר: use (entreaties) | אהרוס: break (down, through) | איננ: in(-curable) | איננ: (father-)less | ישימות: let death seize (from the margin)
(.falsifier: A route in the rendering list that is one group with nothing outside it has no principal word to annex to: 177 routes today ('(put)', '(deal, make)', '(-ing father)'), the provider set each between depth-0 commas, and the store's division at those commas left it with no principal word. They are notation, printed as they stand; see open question 3.

In the head it sits only inside asides in today's routes (259); after the list it is prose (57).

august.said: separates the definition from the KJV rendering list

..means: Three dots inside a rendering: the KJV phrase runs on through words that render other Hebrew words (616). The first depth-0 full stop after the opener ends the rendering list and divides the last rendering from the note after it (108). Elsewhere it closes an abbreviation (126) or a sentence of a note or of the head (68, 6), or is a stray stop inside one rendering (8); none of those divides.
..evidence: יגדיל: great(-er, come to...estate, + things) | ירח: moon. Yrechow | אשכיר: be merry. (Superlative of שָׁקָה.)
..falsifier: A piece after the list's full stop that is a rendering, not a note: 'Ludim. Lydians' and 'landmark. place' read as a stop written for a comma. The division is the same either way; what the second piece is, is open question 1.

-.means: Syllable notation inside one rendering: a suffix that attaches to the end of the principal word (12,118), a prefix that attaches to the start of the next word (2,734), a syllable mark parted from its syllable by a stray space (527), or the hyphen itself as the optional element (3). Between letters, part of a compound or a name (226). Inside the opener, the opener's tail (310; once written after the first rendering, 1). It divides nothing itself; the opener it ends divides.
-.evidence: איננ: in(-curable) | איננ: (father-)less | כדבה: -lying | איננ: well-nigh
-.falsifier: A route whose first character is a hyphen that does not sit in the definition's opener: 21 today ('-or)' 13, '-s' 4, '-th' 4), all suffix syllables. So the head-dash rule reads the definition position, never the route's first character.
-.rule: Not expanded. A syllable is never attached and a group never distributed: 'in(-curable)' stays as written.

wikisource_strongs_explicit_forms.precedence_note: Each divides only at depth 0 and only in its region: the opener divides head from list; the list's full stop divides list from notes; ';' divides in the head and in the list, never in notes or asides; ',' divides only in the list. '(' ')' scope every one of them. '-', '+', 'X', '...', '`', "'", '"', '&', '?', '!', a citation ':' and the Hebrew points never divide.

separates_on.rule: Locate the route in its definition, then cut only at the shapes above, at parenthesis depth 0 and before any unclosed '('. Every piece is kept and is a run of the provider's own characters; the cut characters (and the opener's spaces and dashes) are the mark, not the reading. No piece is joined to another, no group is distributed, no syllable attached, no sign stripped.

open_for_the_owner: 1. Pieces that are not KJV renderings. Where a route runs across the opener, the list's full stop or a head ';', the cut leaves 440 pieces from Strong's own definition (220 etymology-shaped: 'a primitive root', 'from ...', '(Aramaic) corresponding to ...') and 108 notes after the list ('(Superlative of ...)', 'Yrechow', 'Often unexpressed in English'), in 330 routes. Reading A: each prints as a reading, as today's engine already prints the head pieces it cuts at ';'. Reading B: each is kept and printed beside the readings as the provider's definition or note, not as a reading (nothing discarded; the piece carries its region). Some note pieces read as a stop written for a comma ('Ludim. Lydians', 'landmark. place'); those are renderings under either reading.

2. Damaged parentheses. 229 routes print nothing today (sense-split rule 4 with gloss-store holds a damaged sense back) and print whole under the August refusal rule this declaration keeps; 187 come from a definition whose own parentheses do not balance ('selves)', the provider's 'circumcise(-ing), selves)'), 42 from the store cutting through a group the provider closed ('irreg.)', '48 marg)'). Reading A: print whole (August: refusing cost the reader every reading in the row). Reading B: withhold (v3: a text that cannot balance is a text something already edited). A third course, for the 42 only: ask the store to re-cut at the provider's own group.

3. Notation with no principal word. 201 list routes are a syllable or a group standing alone (67 suffix-led: '-s', '-th', '-or)', '(-ing father)'; 177 one group with nothing outside: '(put)', '(deal, make)', '(depart)'), because the provider set them between depth-0 commas and the store divided there. Reading A: print them as they stand. Reading B: the store re-cuts so each stays in one route with the rendering the provider attached it to ('seven(-fold),-s'), which keeps the provider's characters in one run and is a store change, not a page derivation.

4. What '+' means (4,743 occurrences, 4,733 routes). August: 'supplied by the translators and not in the Hebrew'. This declaration: the provider's own sign, a rendering made in connection with one or more other Hebrew words. The store does not carry Strong's 'signs employed' page; the owner confirms from it. The division is the same under both; only the gloss on the sign changes.
5. '&' in the rendering list (18 routes: '& presume', 'lay & to (take a) pledge'): 'and', or a sign (X or +) damaged in transcription. Nothing divides either way.

6. License. The August export line names cc_by_4_0_underlying_public_domain; the store's M14 record says cc_by_sa_4_0_underlying_public_domain (share-alike). This declaration follows the store; the owner confirms, since it governs the export of all 148,506 routes.

7. Routes cut after a chapter:verse colon (45: '3', '10', '18', '48 marg)'): the store took a citation's verse number as a rendering. Today's engine prints 30 and withholds 15 (unbalanced); this declaration prints all 45 whole. Reading A: print, as the provider's characters. Reading B: the store re-cuts the definition with the citation colon read as a citation.
wikisource_strongs_explicit_forms.not_done_here: The definition is never mined for a reading: a route is read where the store cut it, and a head or note piece the store's cut carried in is kept, not swapped for something better. No group is distributed across its head, no syllable is attached, no '+' or 'X' is stripped, no suffix-led or lone-group route is re-joined to the rendering beside it (that is the store's cut to make, at the provider's characters), and nothing is withheld here for damage — whether a damaged route prints is the owner's ruling.
